claim: Tensor parallelism performs one all-reduce per layer per token, making every layer boundary a synchronisation point; on a Gen1/no-P2P fabric the cost is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound because the round trip through host memory costs the same whether the tensor is large or small.
stance_target: the repo's claim that tensor parallelism is ruled out by the fabric
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX, Gen1 x8/x16, no P2P, host-memory-staged collectives; inference (decode) workload
quoted_support: Every layer boundary is a synchronization point: all four ranks block until the slowest one's reduce lands. On a Gen1 fabric with no P2P, that is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound — the round trip through host memory costs the same whether the tensor is large or small.
numbers: one all-reduce per layer per token

claim: Pipeline parallelism performs one hidden-state hand-off per stage boundary instead of one all-reduce per layer, so with N stages there are N-1 hand-offs per token per forward pass, each moving one hidden-state tensor once.
stance_target: the claim that pipeline parallelism is the structurally cheaper topology on a slow fabric, which the repo's 'DDP is the only viable topology' claim omits
quoted_support: With N pipeline stages there are N-1 hand-offs per token per forward pass, each moving one hidden-state tensor once, versus TP's per-layer all-reduce.
numbers: N-1 hand-offs per token per forward pass

claim: On the club's four-card box, GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 with MTP k=3 decoded at 60.4 tok/s at c=1 (median of 5, peak 77.9) and ~38 tok/s aggregate at c=8, while the patched PP4 build reached 87.55 tok/s at c=1 — inverting the earlier verdict so that PP4 became the recipe of record and TP4 was superseded.
stance_target: the claim that tensor parallelism is a usable topology on this fabric at four cards; measured TP4 decode is 60.4 tok/s against PP4's 87.55
scope_conditions: GLM-5.3-Flash AWQ W4A16, four-card CMP 170HX, image ghcr.io/pixelml/...vllm-glm53-sm80-20260903; PP4 numbers measured 2026-09-05 after a 24-patch port
quoted_support: Measured on GLM-5.3-Flash AWQ W4A16, TP4, MTP k=3 ...: **60.4 tok/s c=1 decode (median of 5, peak 77.9)** , **~38 tok/s aggregate decode at c=8** ... With the 24-patch port landed, PP4 + native MTP k=3 measures **87.55 tok/s** c=1 (temp 0, median of 3, clean workload) and **67.91 tok/s** (temp 0.7 + `ignore_eos`, median of 5) against TP4's 60.4

claim: On a two-card bare-metal box at PCIe Gen2 x4 with Intel ACS blocking P2P, PP2 beat TP2+EP on every metric: decode c=1 87.8 vs 69.7 tok/s, prefill 3,610/5,413/5,897 vs 1,388/1,282/1,274 tok/s at ~1.3k/5k/15k tokens, and aggregate 169.8/351.7 vs 110.5/223.6 tok/s at c=4/c=8.
stance_target: the claim that expert parallelism plus tensor parallelism is a viable topology on a Gen2 x4 no-P2P fabric; PP2 wins across decode, prefill and aggregate
scope_conditions: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next AWQ W4A16, 2x CMP 170HX, bare metal Intel X99 CPU root ports, Intel ACS blocks P2P, NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1, cards at Gen2 x4 after cmpunlocker, ~80 W/card, MTP k=3, PLE on CPU offload; one warm run per config, no medians; community-reported via issue #59, not reproduced by the club
quoted_support: TP2's prefill is flat at ~1.3k tok/s across prompt sizes — the comm-bound signature this section predicts — while PP2 scales with chunk size. ... This is the first report that the PP-over-TP direction holds at two cards, on bare metal and on Intel root ports, not only on this club's four-card passthrough box.

claim: On an 8-card PCIe Gen2 x4 box, an 8-stage pipeline's step time follows ~32 ms fixed + 2.1 ms per verified token, and GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 PP8 with DFlash2 k=7 delivered 123 tok/s single-stream on code, 37 tok/s on prose, and 276 tok/s aggregate at 16 concurrent streams.
stance_target: the cost-model shape for pipeline parallelism on the exact Gen2 x4 fabric the query names; carried as the shape of the model, not as a measurement on the club's own hardware
scope_conditions: 8x CMP 170HX at PCIe Gen2 x4, NVFP4 + DFlash2, promisezackr/glm53-flash-170hx-pp8 commit 90ec72e (Apache-2.0, derivative of vLLM); community-reported, not reproduced by the club
quoted_support: measured with per-stage CUDA events on their 8-card PCIe Gen2 x4 box, step time `≈ 32 ms fixed + 2.1 ms × verified tokens per step` ... single-stream decode 123 tok/s (code), 37 tok/s (prose) ... Steady-state aggregate at 16 concurrent streams: 276 tok/s.

claim: At --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 each card spends its whole budget on weights (44.5-45.5 GiB/card for a 14,12,12,7 PP4 partition of a 45-layer model) plus activation and CUDA-graph overhead, leaving negative KV headroom and failing KV-cache allocation; 0.92 fixed it and allocated 1,248,304 KV tokens.
stance_target: the memory-budget arithmetic the repo uses to argue a 7B-total/1B-trainable model fits DDP on 64 GB cards — this is a measured instance of how close to the ceiling a 64 GiB card runs with a large model resident
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX, GLM-5.3-Flash AWQ W4A16, VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,12,12,7 on 45 layers; --max-model-len tried at 524,288 and 262,144, both failed identically
quoted_support: At 0.80, each card spends its whole memory budget (0.80 × 64 GiB) on weights (44.5–45.5 GiB/card for this partition) plus activation/CUDA-graph overhead, leaving no room for KV cache — the engine fails at KV-cache allocation with a negative "Available KV cache memory" value ... Raising `--gpu-memory-utilization` to 0.92 fixed it: KV cache allocated (1,248,304 tokens)

claim: With --enforce-eager the PP4 step time is roughly 160 ms, because enforce-eager disables CUDA-graph capture that on TP4 hides much of the per-step latency.
stance_target: the mechanism behind PP's decode collapse on the unpatched fork — the topology penalty is a latency-hiding problem, not a bandwidth problem
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX, GLM-5.3-Flash AWQ W4A16, PP4 partition 14,12,12,7, --enforce-eager
quoted_support: **`--enforce-eager`PP step time is roughly 160 ms.** Consistent with the c=1 decode collapse above — enforce-eager disables CUDA-graph capture, which on TP4 hides much of the per-step latency; PP4 pays it directly.
numbers: ~160 ms PP step time with enforce-eager

claim: Prefill favours PP4 over TP4 at the same partition: uncached prefill on a ~2,900-token prompt ran 1,053 tok/s on PP4 versus 818 tok/s on TP4, same checkpoint, same box, same day.
stance_target: the claim that tensor parallelism is uniformly better or uniformly worse; the topology advantage is direction-dependent (prefill vs decode)
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX, GLM-5.3-Flash AWQ W4A16, ~2,900-token prompt, measured 2026-09-04
quoted_support: Prefill favors PP4 over TP4 at this partition. Uncached prefill on a ~2,900-token prompt: **1,053 tok/s on PP4 vs 818 tok/s on TP4** , same checkpoint, same box, same day.

claim: A k=0/2/3/5/7 speculative-decoding sweep on the patched PP4 build found draft acceptance falling from 74.0% at k=2 to 37.3% at k=7 while mean accepted length rose only 1.46x, so per-verified-token cost is not flat on this box and k=3 is the throughput record.
stance_target: the hypothesis that a communication-bound box can amortise a fixed per-step cost over a deeper draft; the fixed-cost amortisation argument does not hold because marginal verify cost rises
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX, GLM-5.3-Flash AWQ W4A16, patched PP4 build, measured 2026-09-05
quoted_support: draft acceptance falls from 74.0% at k=2 to 37.3% at k=7 while mean accepted length rises only 1.46x, and the P2 median peaks at k=3 (67.91 tok/s) against 38.13 at k=7. Per-verified-token cost on this box is not flat, so depth does not pay for itself here either.

claim: NVFP4 checkpoints are not viable on SM80: because the card has no native FP4 tensor cores the checkpoint widens on load to roughly 60 GiB resident per card against ~45 GiB of on-disk weight share, and the MoE kernel-format conversion runs out of memory during weight load before any KV budget is computed.
stance_target: the repo's claim that GA100 has no FP8/FP4 tensor cores, and the corollary that quant-format choice on this box is constrained to W4A16/AWQ/Marlin dequant paths
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX, SM80, two attempts on 2026-09-05 with identical signature; memory utilisation 0.90 and 0.85, context lengths 393,216 and 131,072 all failed
quoted_support: because SM80 has no native FP4, the checkpoint widens on load to roughly 60 GiB resident per card against about 45 GiB of weight share on disk, and the mixture-of-experts kernel-format conversion runs out of memory during weight load, before any KV budget is computed. Neither memory utilisation (0.90, 0.85) nor context length (393,216, 131,072) moves it.

claim: The PP-beats-TP argument is expected to transfer to A100 boxes without NVLink because it depends only on the absence of a fast interconnect, but it is untested on A100.
stance_target: the generality of the fabric-driven topology argument beyond CMP 170HX
scope_conditions: Any no-NVLink multi-GPU box; explicitly untested on A100
quoted_support: The same argument — one hand-off per stage boundary beats one all-reduce per layer when there is no fast interconnect — does not depend on anything specific to the CMP 170HX; it applies to any no-NVLink multi-GPU box. Untested on this club's own hardware pool since we have no A100s; carried here as a design hypothesis
